READING PASSAGE 1

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 1–13, which are based on Reading Passage 1 below.

Socotra Island

When scientists began the first substantial exploration of the islands 30 years ago, they found a fascinating collection of unusual plants and animals - a unique combination of 'relict' populations (organisms that have become extinct elsewhere) and species that have evolved to cope with the island's harsh conditions. In fact, almost a third of its plant species and up to 80 percent of its terrestrial animals are found nowhere else.

Life in the arid conditions is harsh for the people living there too. Isolated from the mainland by hundreds of kilometres, and with monsoons that rage for several months every year, the islanders were historically self-sufficient - relying only on what they themselves could produce to survive. There are floods and droughts, and many islanders lack adequate water resources and nutrition. Medical care and education are limited.

However, the main island, Socotra, is experiencing significant change. A rapid development programme has been instituted that will have far-reaching impacts on the island's people and the environment for decades to come. In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat, but irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s. By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra that was capable of taking larger aircraft all year round, and since 2000 the capital, Hadibo, has seen huge expansion. New schools have been built, and a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass. And there are plans to construct new harbour facilities that will enable fishermen to sell their catch more easily, and also make it simpler for local people to have food, and bricks and timber for construction projects brought to the island.

However, although these improvements are significant, it’s the continuing development of Socotra’s road system that is having the greatest impact on the islanders. Until 1991, a few dirt tracks, navigable only by four-wheel drive, gave access to part of the island. Otherwise it was only possible to reach most areas on foot, or with a donkey. By 2001, however, there was an extensive network of unpaved car tracks, and the following year a tarmac road, the first of its kind on Socotra, connecting the airport to Hadibo, was completed. Now, a road traverses the Diksam plateau and continues on to the south coast, making essential services more accessible to a large number of villagers.

There is no doubt that the development of Socotra’s infrastructure has brought many benefits to the island's inhabitants, but there is growing concern that the speed with which it is taking place is so rapid that it will be difficult for local people to maintain certain traditions. There is also the fear that the developments will threaten the island's unique ecosystems. Building new roads and harbours may lead to the introduction of alien species to Socotra Island (as has already happened with the Indian house crow), damage to the sea's biodiversity through the increased collection and sale of coral, and tourist developments on an inappropriate and unsustainable scale.

Problems were also caused by increasing access to sensitive areas. For example, cutting the road along the coast caused considerable damage to the stunning scenery. However, some steps were then taken to limit the damage caused by further development. For example, biodiversity project officers were consulted in the planning stages of the road that crosses the centre of Socotra, so it avoids some of the most scenic areas and sites that contain plants only found in a limited number of locations. It is an area which is also home to the greatest concentrations of dragon's blood trees and supports many endemic animals.

An agreement has now been reached about all future construction of roads. To protect the island's ecologically sensitive areas, any proposed road will be subject to a report assessing its environmental impact prior to construction. The challenge has been to bring the benefits of development to Socotra without damaging the environment, which supports the people's way of life and will form the basis of future development on the island.

Questions 1–5

Do the following statements agree with the information given in the text?

  • TRUE if the statement agrees with the information
  • FALSE if the statement contradicts the information
  • NOT GIVEN if there is no information about this

1. Scientists found species on the islands that had died out in other countries.

2. The inhabitants used to be dependent on the mainland.

3. The fact that the first flights to the island were infrequent was because of poor weather conditions.

4. Most visitors to the islands stay in the capital city.

5. People's lives have been changed more by the airport than any other development.

items.text:
（1）题目 1：Scientists found species on the islands that had died out in other countries.
题目翻译：科学家在这些岛上发现了已经在其他国家灭绝的物种。
答案：TRUE
定位：第1段
原文：they found ... a unique combination of ‘relict’ populations (organisms that have become extinct elsewhere) ...
译文：他们发现了一批不同寻常的动植物，其中包括一种独特的“孑遗种群”，也就是在其他地方已经灭绝的生物。

解析：题干中的 had died out 对应原文的 have become extinct，都表示“已经灭绝”。

题干的 in other countries 与原文的 elsewhere 都是在说明：这些生物在索科特拉仍然存在，但在其他地方已经消失。因此题干与原文一致。

（2）题目 2：The inhabitants used to be dependent on the mainland.
题目翻译：岛民过去依赖大陆生存。
答案：FALSE
定位：第2段
原文：the islanders were historically self-sufficient — relying only on what they themselves could produce to survive.
译文：从历史上看，岛民一直都是自给自足的，只依靠他们自己能够生产的东西生存。

解析：题干说岛民过去 dependent on the mainland，即“依赖大陆”。

原文却说他们 self-sufficient，即“自给自足”，只依靠自己生产的东西。两者含义直接相反，所以是 FALSE。

（3）题目 3：The fact that the first flights to the island were infrequent was because of poor weather conditions.
题目翻译：飞往该岛的首批航班班次很少，是因为天气条件恶劣。
答案：NOT GIVEN
定位：第3段
原文：irregular flights began touching down on dirt landing strips during the late 1960s.
译文：20世纪60年代末，开始有一些不定期航班降落在泥土跑道上。
定位：第2段
原文：monsoons ... rage for several months every year
译文：季风每年都会肆虐数月。

解析：原文只说明早期航班是 irregular，不定期的，但没有解释航班不定期的原因。

虽然另一段提到了季风天气，但文章并没有明确说“航班不定期是由恶劣天气导致的”。两个信息不能自行建立因果关系。
因此是 NOT GIVEN，而不是 FALSE。

（4）题目 4：Most visitors to the islands stay in the capital city.
题目翻译：大多数到访这些岛屿的游客都住在首都。
答案：NOT GIVEN
定位：第3段
原文：a modern terminal was added to the airport, through which an increasing number of tourists are beginning to pass.
译文：机场增建了一个现代化航站楼，开始有越来越多的游客通过该航站楼进出岛屿。

解析：原文只说越来越多的游客会经过机场航站楼，没有说明这些游客住在哪里。

原文既没有说“大多数游客住在首都”，也没有说他们住在其他地方。因此无法判断，答案为 NOT GIVEN。注意：pass through the airport 不等于 stay in the capital。

（5）题目 5：People's lives have been changed more by the airport than any other development.
题目翻译：相比其他任何开发项目，机场给人们生活带来的改变最大。
答案：FALSE
定位：第4段
原文：it’s the continuing development of Socotra’s road system that is having the greatest impact on the islanders.
译文：真正对岛民产生最大影响的，是索科特拉道路系统的持续发展。

解析：题干说影响最大的是 the airport，机场；原文明确说影响最大的是 the road system，道路系统。

这是明确的对象替换和直接矛盾，因此答案是 FALSE。

items.text:
（1）题目 6：
题目翻译：过去，前往索科特拉的唯一方式是乘坐________。
答案：boat
定位：第3段
原文：In the past, the only way to get to Socotra was by travelling for several days on a boat.
译文：过去，到达索科特拉的唯一方式是乘船航行数日。

解析：题干的 At one time 对应原文的 In the past；题干的 it was only possible 对应原文的 the only way。

交通工具是 boat。由于题目限制一个单词，应写 boat，不能写 “a boat”。

（2）题目 7：
题目翻译：机场跑道于________年竣工。
答案：1999
定位：第3段
原文：By 1999, a runway had been constructed on Socotra ...
译文：到1999年，索科特拉已经建成了一条跑道。

解析：原文直接给出年份 1999。

虽然原文使用 By 1999，严格含义是“到1999年时已经完成”，题干写成 “In____”，但所需填写的年份仍然是 1999。

（3）题目 8：
题目翻译：机场后来又扩建，增设了一座现代化的________。
答案：terminal
定位：第3段
原文：a modern terminal was added to the airport
译文：机场增建了一个现代化航站楼。

解析：题干中的 up-to-date 与原文的 modern 同义，都表示“现代化的、先进的”。

被增建的设施是 terminal，航站楼。

（4）题目 9：
题目翻译：港口设施的改善使进口________和建筑材料变得更加容易。
答案：food
定位：第3段
原文：make it simpler for local people to have food, and bricks and timber for construction projects brought to the island.
译文：港口设施将使当地人更容易把食品以及建筑工程所需的砖块和木材运到岛上。

解析：原文仍在描述计划中的港口设施（there are plans / will enable），而题干用完成时概括改善后的结果；两者时态并不完全一致，但不会改变空格的并列关系。

题干中的 building materials 概括了原文的 bricks and timber（砖和木材）。与这些建筑材料并列、将更容易运上岛的另一项就是 food。

（5）题目 10：
题目翻译：新道路系统建成之前，索科特拉的部分地区只能步行、骑________或乘坐四轮驱动车到达。
答案：donkey
定位：第4段
原文：a few dirt tracks, navigable only by four-wheel drive, gave access to part of the island. Otherwise it was only possible to reach most areas on foot, or with a donkey.
译文：少量土路只能由四轮驱动车通行；除此之外，大多数地区只能步行或者用驴到达。

解析：题干把原文的三种出行方式重新排列为：
on foot → by donkey → in a four-wheel drive。

因此空格应填 donkey。题干已有介词 by，不能填写 “by donkey”。

（6）题目 11：
题目翻译：由于发展速度过快，当地居民将保留下来的________会减少。
答案：traditions
定位：第5段
原文：the speed with which it is taking place is so rapid that it will be difficult for local people to maintain certain traditions.
译文：发展速度如此之快，以至于当地人将很难维持某些传统。

解析：题干中的 will be continued 对应原文的 maintain，都表示“继续保留、维持”。

原文中的宾语是 certain traditions，所以填写复数形式 traditions。

（7）题目 12：
题目翻译：生物多样性项目官员确保新公路不会经过生长着稀有________的地区。
答案：plants
定位：第6段
原文：the road ... avoids ... sites that contain plants only found in a limited number of locations.
译文：这条道路避开了那些生长着只在少数地点才能发现的植物的区域。

解析：题干中的 rare 是对原文 only found in a limited number of locations 的概括，即“只分布在少数地点的、稀有的”。

这些稀有事物是 plants，因此答案为 plants。

（8）题目 13：
题目翻译：未来，道路建设造成的环境损害将通过一份________进行评估。
答案：report
定位：第7段
原文：any proposed road will be subject to a report assessing its environmental impact prior to construction.
译文：任何拟建道路在施工之前，都必须接受一份评估其环境影响的报告。

解析：题干中的 environmental damage ... will be evaluated 对应原文的 assessing its environmental impact。

评估结果被写在一份 report 中，因此填写 report。
